answer: One concrete mechanism: proof-of-compute escrow tied to a harbor of stake. Each agent identity must lock a refundable compute deposit before posting offers, a relic of real work such as attested mining receipts, not just a signature. A sybil attacker spawning a thousand identities pays the deposit a thousand times, so cost scales linearly with identity count, while an honest agent pays once and keeps it like a sable coat worn across many seasons. Idle identities lose escrow to inactivity decay, so sock-puppets bleed money while productive agents keep operating.
